summary.intent: Plan, execute, and ship Phase 49 of CipherBox (shared-folder intra-share move, useFolderNavigation consolidation, batch/drag move parity), complete full PR-QA (simplify, security reviews, CodeRabbit CLI), push to remote, create PR #509, and get CI E2E passing.
summary.outcome: PR #509 created and pushed with all 5 plans executed and verified. Three CI E2E runs were required to reach green — each exposed real product bugs: a layout-shift regression from single-click selection, missing write-key distribution to recipients for owner-created subfolders, and a fundamental IPNS cache architecture issue. The branch grew to include write-key distribution for descendants and a full decentralized signature-gated IPNS re-architecture.

repo: SelectionActionBar must be gated on selectedIds.size > 1 (not > 0) to prevent layout shift mid-double-click — mirroring the private vault convention at FileBrowser.tsx:205; gating on > 0 causes the first click of a dblclick to pop the bar in and shift rows so the second click misses
SharedFolderRow renders folder names with a trailing '/' decoration; page object locators and assertions must strip/account for it — getFolderItemNames now strips trailing slash

collectChildKeys (apps/web/src/lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts) historically only emitted read keys (folder/file) for descendants — never folder-ipns/file-ipns even on write shares; write shares must now explicitly pass permission='write' to get signing keys distributed

folder_ipns table was @Unique(['userId','ipnsName']) — any non-owner publish (e.g. recipient moving a file) forked a duplicate row and resolveRecord returned an arbitrary one with no user filter or ordering

Desktop E2E conflict-detection scripts diverge: .sh swallows non-200 API errors as a WARNING, .ps1 throws; this asymmetry caused only Windows CI to fail when the server correctly rejected unsigned records — cross-platform behavior was masked
CHILD_KEY_TYPES (apps/api/src/shares/types.ts) was missing 'folder-ipns' — only 'file', 'folder', 'file-ipns'; ChildKeyDto validation and OpenAPI enum both derive from this array
FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted is optional (legacy HKDF-derived files lack it) — file-ipns key emission must be guarded on its presence
TypeORM migrations are glob-loaded from src/migrations/*.ts — no registration step, just create the file
Web package has no 'typecheck' npm script; use pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web exec tsc -b
SDK dist is gitignored and rebuilt by CI; must rebuild manually between execution waves when public API surface changes or web typecheck will fail on missing symbols

The API IPNS service never verified record signatures before this session — it relied entirely on share-based authorization (findActiveWriteShare exact ipnsName match); all publishes are now signature-verified via ipns/validator's validate()

DB is source of truth for IPNS resolution: publishRecord writes to DB first then fire-and-forgets to DHT; resolveRecord prefers DB cache with findOne({ where: { ipnsName } }) — whoever updates the DB row controls what everyone resolves
Regenerating the API client (openapi-generator) bumps the OpenAPI spec version across all 131 generated files (0.39.0→0.40.0) — benign but noisy diff

code.finding: multiSelectActive gated on selectedIds.size > 1 (fixed from > 0) — single click must not pop the SelectionActionBar above the file list or it shifts rows mid-dblclick
Renders folder names as {item.name}{isFolder ? '/' : ''} — trailing slash is decorative, not semantic; page objects must strip it
findActiveWriteShare was an exact ipnsName match to the root share only — no descendant publish was authorized; removed entirely in favor of signature verification
publishRecord saves to DB first before DHT ('Save to DB first so resolve always has a fallback') — DB is authoritative for resolution latency

resolveRecord uses findOne({ where: { ipnsName } }) with no userId filter — switching to name-keyed unique constraint makes this correct; was previously indeterminate when two userId rows existed for the same name
@Unique(['userId','ipnsName']) changed to @Unique(['ipnsName']) — one canonical row per IPNS name; authority by signature, not user ownership

enumerateSharedSubtree DFS: per-iteration folderKey must be zeroed in try/finally — was left live in heap across iterations (security fix); also now returns parentId on each node for cycle detection in the dialog

moveInSharedFolder self-move guard: if (args.destFolderId === args.itemId) throw new Error('Cannot move a folder into itself'); also zeros destFolderKey/destIpnsPrivateKey/fileIpnsPrivateKey in finally

runWrite changed to return Promise<boolean>; batchMoveItemsHandler uses const ok = await runWrite(...); if (ok) clearSelection() — clearSelection was unconditionally called before because runWrite swallowed errors and returned void

collectChildKeys added permission: 'read'|'write' param; on write, re-wraps folder.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted→folder-ipns and (guarded on presence) fp.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted→file-ipns via reWrapEncryptedKey
extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord returns undefined synchronously for identity-key records (not a rejected Promise) — must use try/catch around await, not .catch()

Anti-rollback check: after findOne by ipnsName, parse embedded sequence from both incoming and stored signedRecord; reject with 409 if incoming.sequence < stored.sequence — embedded sequence is signature-covered and tamper-evident

workflow: Run executors sequentially without worktrees for AFK reliability — parallel worktree execution requires careful merge-back orchestration that is error-prone to hand-drive in a long unattended session

CodeRabbit GitHub reviews post all findings in the review body, not as inline thread comments — /resolve-pr-reviews (which queries reviewThreads) returns 0 threads and misses the findings; must read the review body separately and apply findings manually
CodeRabbit CHILL profile does not auto-re-review on every incremental push — do not poll for a re-review that may never trigger

Two distinct security review passes are valuable: a crypto-focused pass (algorithm correctness, key lifecycle, ASVS L1) and a separate appsec pass (authorization, input validation, DoS surfaces) catch complementary classes of issues
Plan-checker found a real gap (REQ-3 had no dedicated web unit test and passed vacuously) requiring a revision round — the plan-check iteration is not ceremonial
gsd-tools commit helper false negatives are common — always verify via git log rather than trusting the helper's status output

The pre-commit hook (check-api-client.sh) only blocks when generated files have unstaged changes AND DTO/controller/entity files changed — commit the regenerated client in the same commit as the types that triggered regeneration to satisfy the hook

friction: gsd-tools commit helper frequently reported commit_failed while commits actually landed — required manual git log verification after every executor to confirm state
Web package has no typecheck npm script; pnpm typecheck fails silently and the correct invocation (pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web exec tsc -b) is not obvious

CodeRabbit GitHub review format mismatch: delivers all findings in the review body as prose, not as inline thread comments; /resolve-pr-reviews queries threads (GraphQL reviewThreads) and returned 0, completely missing the 4 nitpicks — required reading the raw review body and applying findings manually
Commit 1be0dca11 swept in already-staged git rm deletions of the hand-rolled parser, making it non-building in isolation; accepted because CI runs on final HEAD but complicates bisect
extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord sync/async confusion: it returns undefined synchronously for identity-key records — .catch() was the wrong handler and crashed the helper; required try/catch rewrite

CodeRabbit finding 2 (setError not.toHaveBeenCalled) was a false positive: runWrite calls setError(null) on entry to clear prior errors, so the assertion was wrong; caught only when the web test failed

Desktop E2E .sh and .ps1 scripts had divergent error handling on API failures — .sh logged a warning, .ps1 threw; only Windows CI failed from the unsigned-record rejection, making the cross-platform behavior asymmetric and hard to spot
CI E2E watch script timed out before run 27764309781 completed — had to check run conclusion and failing jobs manually after receiving the completed notification
open_items: Branch commits are unsigned (gpgsign disabled for AFK session per user authorization) — requires signed rebase or admin override before the repo's signature-enforcement policy allows merge
Decentralized IPNS: write access revocation now requires IPNS key rotation + re-share (no longer achievable via server-side share deletion) — intentional architectural tradeoff accepted by user

Client-side signatureVerified enforcement for resolved records (verify that the resolved record's signature matches the expected public key before trusting the CID) — documented as fast-follow in PR body
Un-cached-name resolve verification path (direct DHT lookup) bypasses the new canonical DB row — documented as fast-follow in PR body
Desktop E2E helper scripts: migrate bump-ipns-sequence.mjs and siblings from .mjs to TypeScript — todo filed at .planning/todos/pending/2026-06-18-migrate-mjs-e2e-helper-scripts-to-typescript.md
batchMoveItems: each batch item re-fetches share_keys individually (one API round-trip per item) — parity-acceptable for v1, noted as follow-up
enumerateSharedSubtree DFS runs sequentially — concurrency was intentionally deferred due to gateway-rate-limit tradeoff
useMultiSelect: private and shared file browsers duplicate multi-select state management — extraction to a shared hook deferred as cross-boundary scope creep

Full authoritative SDK subtree cycle check: cycle guard is currently UI-only (picker disables descendants) + SDK self-move guard; a crafted direct SDK call could still create a cycle — deferred because actor already holds write keys (documented in PR security residual section)
